newsitem.title: USA: Midwest Cash Grain PM - Soy, corn sales stay slow.
newsitem.headline: Midwest Cash Grain PM - Soy, corn sales stay slow.

text.p: Soybean and corn sales in U.S. cash grain markets were slow on Tuesday despite sharply higher prices in some CBOT contracts, grain merchandisers said.
"They've held on to the grain this long, they might as well hang on to it a little longer," said one eastern Corn Belt dealer.
"At one point, everybody was promising $9.00, $10.00 and $12.00 (per bushel) soybeans.
CBOT July soybeans ended 35-1/4 cents per bushel higher at $7.68, and August was up 25 at $7.22. July corn ended up 2-3/4 cents per bushel higher at $2.43-1/4.
One dealer in Indiana speculated that his terminal would not see heavy soybean sales until old crop months climbed back up to $8.00 per bushel.
Basis bids in Toledo, Ohio jumped a bit, but dealers there said the move was made in response to the way the July/August spread widened to 46 cents per bushel.
Weather through much of the U.S. Midwest was favorable and should keep prices in check in the long term, dealers said.
Basis values are quoted against CBOT futures, cash $/bu.
